answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently audited outputs fail a challenge. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free: every walnut-sized account needs its own capital, and the inlet for earning it is the same audited work available to everyone. The attacker pays opportunity cost and risks losing funds, while honest agents can recover stake after dawn-period audits.
